rationale: The student can isolate individual phonemes but struggles to blend them into a whole word. The 'blend' mode directly isolates this missing skill by having the student hear sequential phonemes and synthesize them into a whole spoken word.
intent: Generate short-vowel CVC phoneme-blending exercises where the child hears three segmented sounds (e.g., /s/ /a/ /t/, /p/ /i/ /n/) and blends them into the target word. Do not include 'mat' to avoid giving away the current reading task answer directly, keeping within simple Grade 1 short vowels (e.g., short a). Focus strictly on smooth auditory synthesis without isolated letter stopping.

data.title: Sound Safari: Reading short-vowel CVC words

judgement.reasoning: The student can segment sounds (/m/ /a/ /t/) but struggles with auditory synthesis (blending them into a word). The chosen detour shifts to oral phoneme blending (Sound Blend mode) without print overload, isolating the prerequisite skill of smooth blending.
judgement.verdict: Yes, this directly targets oral phoneme blending to help the student synthesize sounds before returning to blending printed letters in the reader.
